q: What comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___ ?

m: There are 20 odd numbers; their sum is 20 × 20.

q: 3/4 of a number is 27. What is 2/3 of the same number?
m: 1/4 is 9, so the number is 36. 2/3 of 36 = 24.

q: Arrange from smallest to largest: 0.6, 5/8, 7/12, 0.65
Aarav and Ben have ₹240 altogether. Aarav has ₹40 more than Ben. How much does Ben have (₹)?
m: Bar model: remove the extra ₹40, then split: (240 − 40) ÷ 2.

q: A batsman scored 45, 62 and 38 in three innings. How many runs must he score in the 4th innings to average 50?
A cricket bat costs ₹800. With a 15% discount, what is the price (₹)?
Red and blue bricks are in the ratio 3 : 5. There are 64 bricks. How many more blue bricks than red?
m: 8 units = 64, so 1 unit = 8. Blue − red = 2 units = 16.

q: A car travels 150 km in 2.5 hours. At the same speed, how many hours will 210 km take?
What is the smallest number greater than 1 that leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6?
How many whole numbers from 1 to 100 are divisible by 3 or 5 (or both)?
AB and BA are 2-digit numbers (A and B are digits). AB + BA = 121 and A − B = 5. What is AB?
m: AB + BA = 11(A + B) = 121, so A + B = 11. With A − B = 5: A = 8, B = 3.

q: Amit, Bala, Chirag and Dev ran a race. Bala finished behind Amit but ahead of Chirag. Dev finished immediately after Amit. Who finished third?
m: The order must be Amit, Dev, Bala, Chirag.

q: How many different 3-digit numbers can be made from 1, 2, 3, 4 with no digit repeated?
8 friends each shake hands once with every other friend. How many handshakes?
m: Each of 8 shakes 7 hands, but each handshake is counted twice: 8 × 7 ÷ 2.

q: A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm × 4 cm square cut from one corner. What is the perimeter of the remaining shape (cm)?
m: The cut edges just move inward, so the perimeter stays 2 × (12 + 8) = 40.

q: One angle of a triangle is 60°. Of the other two angles, one is twice the other. What is the largest angle (degrees)?
m: The other two share 120° as 1 : 2, so they are 40° and 80°.

q: A 3 × 3 × 3 cube is painted on all sides and cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly 2 painted faces?
m: One cube sits in the middle of each of the 12 edges.

q: I think of a number, multiply by 3, subtract 7, then divide by 2. I get 10. What was my number?
A farm has chickens and rabbits: 20 heads and 56 legs. How many rabbits?
m: If all 20 were chickens: 40 legs. 16 extra legs ÷ 2 extra per rabbit = 8 rabbits.
Put 3 + 7 = 10 between the digits and carry: 407.

q: The digits of a 2-digit number add up to 9. The number is 27 more than the number with its digits reversed. What is the number?
m: Reversing changes it by 9 × (difference of digits), so the digits differ by 3 and add to 9: 6 and 3.

q: Write 0.375 as a fraction in simplest form.
Riya spent 1/4 of her money on a book, then 1/3 of the rest on a pen. She has ₹120 left. How much did she have at first (₹)?
m: After the book 3/4 is left; the pen takes 1/3 of that = 1/4. Half is left = ₹120, so she had ₹240.

q: Which is larger?
Write 0.625 as a fraction in simplest form.
A tank is 2/5 full. After 30 litres are added it is 4/5 full. What is its capacity (litres)?
m: 4/5 − 2/5 = 2/5 of the tank = 30 litres, so 1/5 = 15 and the tank holds 75.

q: Which is smaller?

m: Each term is 1/n − 1/(n+1), so the total is 1 − 1/10.

q: 1 1/2 + 2 2/3 = ? (you can write a mixed number like 4 1/6)
Which fraction is exactly halfway between 1/3 and 1/2?
Meera ate 2/7 of a cake. Raj ate 1/3 of what was left. What fraction of the cake remains?
m: 5/7 was left; Raj ate 1/3 of it, leaving 2/3 of 5/7 = 10/21.

q: A rope is cut: first 1/4 of it, then 1/3 of what remains, then 1/2 of what remains. 6 m is left. How long was the rope (m)?
m: Left: 3/4 → 2/3 of that = 1/2 → half of that = 1/4. 1/4 = 6 m, so 24 m.

q: Which is the greatest?
Two numbers add up to 50 and their difference is 14. What is the larger number?
A has 3 times as many cards as B. Together they have 84. How many does A have?
Ravi has ₹50 more than Sam. Ravi gives Sam ₹15. Now how much more does Ravi have than Sam (₹)?
A pen and a book cost ₹90 together. The book costs ₹30 more than 2 pens. How much is the book (₹)?
m: Pen = 1 unit, book = 2 units + 30. 3 units + 30 = 90, so 1 unit = 20 and the book is 70.

q: Ali had twice as many marbles as Bo. After Ali gave Bo 12 marbles, they had the same number. How many did Ali have at first?
m: The gap was 1 unit and giving 12 closes 24, so 1 unit = 24. Ali had 2 units = 48.

q: Two numbers add up to 72 and their difference is 18. What is the smaller number?
A mother is 4 times as old as her son. Their ages add up to 60. How old is the son?
Priya has ₹80 more than Tia. Priya gives Tia ₹25. Now how much more does Priya have (₹)?
3 bats and 2 balls cost ₹1,300. 1 bat and 2 balls cost ₹500. How much is 1 bat (₹)?
m: The difference is 2 bats = ₹800, so 1 bat = ₹400.

q: Jay had 3 times as many stickers as Kim. After Jay gave Kim 20, they had the same. How many did Kim have at first?
m: The gap was 2 units; giving 20 closes 40, so 2 units = 40 and Kim had 1 unit = 20.

q: Three consecutive numbers add up to 81. What is the largest?
A school has 480 pupils. There are 60 more girls than boys. How many girls?
A and B share ₹600. A gets ₹60 more than twice what B gets. How much does B get (₹)?
m: B = 1 unit, A = 2 units + 60. 3 units = 540, so 1 unit = 180.

q: 4 pens and 3 rulers cost ₹62. 2 pens and 3 rulers cost ₹46. How much is one pen (₹)?
A box has 30 balls, red and white. If 4 red balls were painted white, there would be equal numbers. How many red balls?
Kabir has 3 times as many runs as Dev. If Kabir scores 10 more and Dev scores 30 more, they will be equal. How many runs does Kabir have now?
m: The gap of 2 units = 30 − 10 = 20, so 1 unit = 10 and Kabir has 30.

q: 3, 7, 11, 15, … What is the 20th term?

m: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13.

100, 97, 94, 91, … What is the 18th term?
The pattern A, B, C, D, E, A, B, C, … repeats. What is the 100th letter?
m: 100 ÷ 5 leaves remainder 0, so it is the last letter of a block: E.

q: Dots are arranged in rows: 1 dot, then 2, then 3, and so on. How many dots in the first 12 rows?
What is the units digit of 2²⁰ (2 multiplied by itself 20 times)?
m: Units digits cycle 2, 4, 8, 6. 20 is a multiple of 4, so it ends in 6.

q: What is the HCF of 36 and 48?
What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
m: Multiples of 18: 18, 36 — and 36 is a multiple of 12.

Which digit goes in the box so that 4□72 is divisible by 9?
m: Digit sum 4 + 7 + 2 = 13; the next multiple of 9 is 18, so the digit is 5.

The 3-digit number 5□6 is divisible by 4. What is the smallest digit that can go in the box?
m: The last two digits must be divisible by 4: 16 works.

How many 2-digit numbers are divisible by 7?
What is the sum of all the factors of 28?
Batting order: Rohan bats before Sid. Sid bats before Tom. Uday bats after Sid and right before Tom. Who bats third?
m: The only order that fits is Rohan, Sid, Uday, Tom.

Box A says 'The prize is in here.' Box B says 'The prize is not in here.' Box C says 'The prize is not in Box A.' Exactly one box tells the truth. Where is the prize?
m: Test each: only 'prize in B' makes exactly one statement (C's) true.

q: In how many ways can you make exactly ₹10 using only ₹2 and ₹5 coins?
m: Five ₹2 coins, or two ₹5 coins. One ₹5 would leave ₹5, which ₹2 coins can't make.

Today is Wednesday. What day will it be 100 days from today?

A snail climbs 3 m up a 10 m wall each day and slips back 2 m each night. On which day does it reach the top?
m: After 7 days and nights it is at 7 m. On day 8 it climbs 3 m and reaches 10 m before slipping.
